title: Infrastructure and Recovery Architecture
summary: Pinned stack, recovery USB, eMMC imaging, services, permissions, and rollback model.

content.text: Plain summary

The migration is designed like a reversible appliance conversion. First prove that we can boot recovery, identify the exact screen hardware, image the entire eMMC, verify the backup, and restore it. Only after that should mainline be written.
Pinned stack
Base OS target: Armbian for MKS-Klipad50, recorded in stack.lock.json.
Production Klipper pin: v0.13.0 at commit 61c0c8d2ef40340781835dd53fb04cc7a454e37a.
Moonraker, Mainsail, KlipperScreen, Crowsnest, KAMP subset, and timelapse components are pinned by source, version, hash, and compatibility notes.
Non-deploying next compatibility is separated from the stable production pin.
KIAUH-style interactive updates are deliberately not part of production.
Recovery foundation
Use the existing USB stick for recovery boot preparation and direct Ethernet for image transfer.
Before any eMMC write, confirm screen identity, block layout, U-Boot identity, and that root is running from USB recovery.
Capture the whole eMMC, record geometry and hashes, validate compressed and raw data, and loop-mount read-only for inspection.
Keep Comgrow 1.5.2 restorable from the laptop.
All destructive write commands are guarded by recovery markers, size checks, machine identity checks, --apply, and typed confirmation.
Official stock recovery artifacts

Downloaded on 2026-08-05 from the firmware folder linked by Sovol's official T300 support page: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rFLPNeZ_xBWPsWQtqwa89L1O_wsu9wDe. The files are stored outside Git in /home/devianttoaster/Downloads/T300-Private-Recovery-20260805 with a mode-700 directory and mode-600 files. Google Drive's listed byte counts matched every completed download.
Comgrow_T300_V1.5.2_20240316.img: 6,738,149,376 bytes; SHA-256 7fe893c9a5f2a8f64500f7fc1f1681c48754c7665c4215f5fdc0395b922de3ba. It contains a 256 MiB FAT partition and a 6 GiB Linux partition.
Screen_firmware_V1.5.2.tft: 9,668,308 bytes; SHA-256 7326ce53567553f4b7fa7b6d64fcf714d901be905f49e2e05548f4af9aafba4e.
zc_app.deb: 161,684,496 bytes; SHA-256 0e3953bde38cc0cbe40cb7dc08ec6f1d4aeafb42fe820a21f54a51777d647513. Its Debian archive contains debian-binary, control.tar.xz, and data.tar.xz.

The empty owner-only destination reserved for this printer's exact eMMC capture is /home/devianttoaster/T300-Private-Backups/stock-1.5.2-20260805. The recovery session will create the compressed image and manifest there only after board identity, root-on-USB, and unmounted-eMMC checks pass.
These files improve rollback preparedness but do not replace the required byte-for-byte eMMC capture from this exact printer. Do not run or flash any of them during ordinary recovery inspection.
Service model

Klipper, Moonraker, Mainsail, KlipperScreen, Crowsnest, admission scanning, host MCU, and display support are staged as separate services with narrow writable directories, resource limits, and explicit device access. Camera, network, and storage failures must degrade those features without blocking emergency shutdown or printer safety.
Why this design

The stock firmware works but mixes vendor macros, power-loss recovery, touchscreen assumptions, and hidden state. Rebuilding the stack from pinned sources gives us a base where safety decisions, updates, and rollback are visible instead of guessed.
